The parameters a declared model would spend, counted before it is fitted

Source: R/modeling_rms.R
mm_parameter_budget.Rd

A categorical predictor spends one parameter per level after the first, a continuous one spends one, a spline spends knots - 1, and an interaction spends the product of what its two sides spend. Counting it beforehand is what makes it possible to refuse a model that cannot be estimated instead of waiting for rms::lrm() to grind through a design matrix wider than the cohort is long.

Usage

mm_parameter_budget(
  project,
  frame,
  nonlinear = NULL,
  knots = 4L,
  pairs = list()
)

Arguments

project

A mm_project().

frame

The rows that would be fitted.

nonlinear, knots, pairs

The shape, as mm_model() resolved it.

Value

A list with total and the per-predictor spent.

Details

The case this exists for is an identifier offered as a predictor. A column with one level per row spends n - 1 parameters, saturates the model on its own, and takes a long time to fail. The rule here is exact rather than a threshold: a model whose parameters reach the number of rows has nothing left to estimate them with.
